response:
Standings diagnosis. Four signals now cluster at −4.0% to −4.7% FF5 alpha with t ≈ −3.4 to −4.0 and FMB ≈ −2.1 to −2.9, and all four share the same core: a **capacity-expansion carrier × internal-funding-shortfall quality leg**. Neither profit-gating, nor merging with solvency slack, nor weakest-link aggregation beat the original gen-1 construct, so the mechanism is identified and the remaining gains must come from *measurement* of its two legs, not from further conditioning layers. Three things are demonstrably suboptimal in the leading signal: (i) coverage is only 0.076 because oancf restricts the sample, (ii) GROWTH(ppegt,1) is explosive for asset-light firms and undefined for firms with tiny gross PP&E, and (iii) the shortfall is scaled by assets rather than by the investment programme it is supposed to fund. Signals 1–3 and 6 address exactly these, while 4–5 test two genuinely untested demand- and cost-side quality channels on the proven carrier.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Capacity growth against internal funds with FFO fallback
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(GROWTH(ppegt, 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(capx, COALESCE(oancf, ADD(ib, dp))), at), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: The funding-shortfall mechanism is about internal cash generation, not about which statement reports it; using funds from operations wherever the cash-flow statement is unavailable should preserve the economics while materially widening the sample the signal can trade.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The leading construct trades on only 7.6% of firm-months because oancf is unavailable for early years and for some filers, and funds from operations (earnings plus depreciation) is the standard economic substitute used before cash-flow statements existed — a justified missing-data convention rather than a coverage patch. If alpha and slope hold with materially higher coverage, the mechanism becomes far more credible; if they deteriorate, we learn the effect is specific to true operating cash flow rather than to accrual-based internal funds.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Asset-scaled capital formation against funding shortfall
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(ppegt, 1), LAG(at, 1)), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(capx, oancf), at), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: How much new productive capital a firm adds relative to its whole asset base is a more comparable measure of expansion than the percentage growth of its existing property account, which is mechanically explosive for asset-light firms and meaningless for firms with almost no gross PP&E.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This changes only the measurement of the carrier — gross capacity addition scaled by lagged total assets instead of a percentage growth rate — putting the investment leg on the same denominator as the funding-gap leg so the interaction compares like with like. It should stabilize the extreme portfolios (the growth-rate version's top decile is dominated by tiny-PPE firms) and thereby improve the Sharpe and t-statistics without altering the economic claim.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Capacity growth with weak internal coverage of capex
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(GROWTH(ppegt, 1)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf, capx)))))
HYPOTHESIS: The economically meaningful quantity is what fraction of the investment programme operations actually pay for; a firm spending twice its operating cash flow is externally dependent regardless of how large that gap looks relative to total assets.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Normalizing internal cash by the investment programme rather than by the asset base removes the capital-intensity and size contamination in the (capx − oancf)/at scaling, and ranking the coverage ratio before standardizing handles the sign and scale pathologies that arise when operating cash flow is negative. This is a different economic normalization of the winning channel, not a rescaling of the same variable, so a comparison directly tests which funding metric the market prices.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Capacity growth into decelerating demand
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(GROWTH(ppegt, 1)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(DELTA(GROWTH(sale, 1), 1), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Capacity commitments are made on extrapolated demand; firms that add capacity just as their revenue growth decelerates have misjudged the cycle and will operate the new assets below plan, whereas firms adding capacity into accelerating demand are responding to genuine absorption.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The quality gauge is the *acceleration* of the revenue base — a demand-momentum concept the archive has never tested, distinct from margin levels, trends, cash flow, or receivables quality — and it captures the timing error that turns investment unproductive. Both legs are dense one-year quantities, so coverage should be well above the leading signal's 0.076.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Capacity growth with unit-cost inflation
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(GROWTH(ppegt, 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(GROWTH(cogs, 1), GROWTH(sale, 1)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: When cost of goods grows faster than revenue, each incremental unit sold is less profitable; expanding capacity in that state adds volume to deteriorating unit economics, whereas expanding while costs grow slower than sales scales a widening spread.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The cost-versus-revenue growth wedge is a flow measure of deteriorating unit economics that is immune to the level and industry-mix problems of gross-margin ratios and is not spanned by the cash-flow, solvency, or receivables channels already tested. Paired with the proven capacity-growth carrier, it isolates whether *operating* deterioration, as opposed to *financing* fragility, also makes expansion unproductive.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Multi-year net capital formation against funding shortfall
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(SUB(capx, dp), 3), LAG(at, 1)), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(capx, oancf), at), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Genuine expansion is capital spending in excess of capital consumption sustained over several years; firms that have been adding net capital for three years while still failing to fund investment internally are the clearest cases of persistent, externally financed overexpansion.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The carrier becomes cumulative *net* capital formation (capex less depreciation over three years, asset-scaled), which strips replacement investment and single-year lumpiness from the expansion measure — a different investment state variable than either a one-year growth rate or a gross cumulative capex total. Holding the funding-gap leg unchanged keeps the comparison to the leading signal clean and tests whether persistence of net capital formation, rather than the current year's expansion, is the operative investment condition.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---CRITIQUE Capacity growth against internal funds with FFO fallback---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is the archive's leading signal (generation-1 "Financing-deficit-weighted capacity growth") with a COALESCE data-fallback bolted on — a coverage patch rather than a new economic condition, and one whose ib+dp substitute is itself unlikely to be populated where oancf is missing, so the expected gain in tradable breadth is speculative while the mechanism is unchanged.

---CRITIQUE Asset-scaled capital formation against funding shortfall---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: By the proposer's own admission this "changes only the measurement of the carrier," i.e. it re-scales GROWTH(ppegt,1) to Δppegt/lag(at) in the already-tested leading interaction, and the archive has separately tested exactly this asset-scaled capacity-addition construct ("Capacity added beyond internal funding capacity"), so it is a cosmetic normalization variant rather than a substantive improvement.

---CRITIQUE Capacity growth with weak internal coverage of capex---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Re-normalizing internal funds by the investment programme instead of by assets is a defensible alternative measurement of the winning channel with a coherent sign, but it remains the same economic mechanism, the IND_ZSCORE(IND_RANK(...)) nesting is redundant, and oancf/capx is pathological for near-zero-capex firms (huge "coverage" scores assigned to firms whose PP&E grew by acquisition rather than capex).

---CRITIQUE Capacity growth into decelerating demand---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: Revenue-growth acceleration is a genuinely untested quality leg in this archive (distinct from margin levels/trends, cash flow, turnover, and receivables), the expansion-timing-error mechanism is economically coherent, the sign direction matches the expression, and both legs are dense; the main caveat is that part of the result may load on the standalone sales-acceleration effect rather than the interaction.

---CRITIQUE Capacity growth with unit-cost inflation---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The cogs-minus-sales growth wedge is algebraically close to a one-year change in gross margin, a leg already tested twice in this archive (margin-validated capex expansion, labor bloat with margin compression, capex into a multi-year gross-profitability decline) with weak results, so this is a repackaging of the margin-deterioration channel rather than a new one.

---CRITIQUE Multi-year net capital formation against funding shortfall---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Cumulative net-of-depreciation capital formation is a legitimately different investment state variable from either a one-year growth rate or the gross five-year capex sum already tested, and the sign logic is internally consistent, but it overlaps with the previously tested capx/dp and TS_SUM(capx,5) carriers and will push coverage below the leading signal's already-thin 0.076.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Hiring commitments against internal funding shortfall
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(GROWTH(emp, 1), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(capx, oancf), at), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Headcount growth is the least reversible investment a firm makes — wages must be paid every period and layoffs are costly — so hiring while investment already exceeds internal cash generation commits the firm to a fixed cash burden it cannot fund, whereas cash-generative firms can carry new staff through a slow patch.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This replaces the coverage patch with a substantively different investment channel: the carrier is an off-balance-sheet, irreversible labor commitment rather than capitalized property, which tests whether the funding-fragility mechanism is about capital formation specifically or about committing to any fixed obligation without internal funds. Employment is reported far more broadly and uniformly than gross PP&E, so tradable breadth improves for an economic reason rather than through a missing-data substitution.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Expanding at peak own-history profitability
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(GROWTH(ppegt, 1)), IND_ZSCORE(TS_RANK(RATIO(ib, at), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: Managers extrapolate temporarily good results: capacity added when profitability stands at the top of the firm's own five-year range is capacity built on a cyclical peak that will mean-revert, whereas expansion undertaken when profitability is at the low end of its own history reflects deliberate counter-cyclical investment.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This reverses the usual conditioning logic — it is not low profitability but *transitorily high* profitability that makes expansion unproductive — and it may explain why cross-sectional profitability levels produced slopes without alpha in this archive, since a high level relative to peers is not the same as a high level relative to the firm's own norm. TS_RANK is bounded and firm-normalized, so it introduces no outlier or industry-mix contamination into the interaction.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Capacity growth during an inventory glut
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(GROWTH(ppegt, 1)), IND_ZSCORE(TS_RANK(RATIO(invt, sale), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: Inventory sitting at a multi-year high relative to sales means the firm cannot clear what it already produces; adding productive capacity in that state compounds an existing glut, while expanding when stock is lean relative to sales indicates demand genuinely pulling product through.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: The quality gauge is the firm's own inventory-to-sales *position in its five-year history* — a demand-absorption state rather than the one-year inventory-versus-sales growth wedge or a margin change, so it is not a repackaging of the margin-deterioration channel the critic identified. It is bounded, firm-normalized, and densely available, and it pairs a working-capital state with the physical-capacity carrier that has produced the archive's largest alphas.
